correctness.rationale: The homogeneous ball/sphere mean identity, the sign of the first nonzero Taylor term of Delta log u, and the exponential expansion through degree 2m give an explicit negative leading coefficient for p<1+2m/n. The m=1 specialization matches Mochizuki's published second-order coefficient, and homogeneous harmonic germs give the stated sharpness above the threshold.

originality.rationale: Mochizuki 2005 leaves the intermediate range open beyond a Delta u(a)>0 criterion. Ekonen-Kinnunen-Marola-Sbordone 2009 gives a global result only through exponent n/(n-1). Searches of finite-jet, real-analytic, flatness, Pizzetti, log-subharmonic and equivalent mean-value terminology did not locate the finite-order threshold or infinite-flatness obstruction. Originality is to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem settles the entire local intermediate range for positive real-analytic log-subharmonic functions and reduces any smooth positive counterexample to the highly degenerate infinite-order-flat case. It also supplies a sharp jet-dependent exponent 1+2m/n.

limitations: The theorem is local and assumes positivity near the point.
Zeros of log-subharmonic functions are not treated.
The endpoint p=1+2m/n is not classified in general.
Equivalent prior coverage under higher-order Pizzetti or mean-value terminology remains a residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
